question:
A container has a \(1 \times 1\) square bottom, a \(3 \times 3\) open square top, and four congruent trapezoidal sides, as shown. Starting when the container is empty, a hose that runs water at a constant rate takes \(35\) minutes to fill the container up to the midline of the trapezoids.

[Figure 1](figures/2025_AMC_12B_Q15_question_fig1.svg)

How many more minutes will it take to fill the remainder of the container?
solution:
At a constant flow rate, filling time is proportional to water volume. We therefore need the ratio of the volumes above and below the trapezoids' midlines, rather than the container's actual height.

[Figure 1](figures/2025_AMC_12B_Q15_question_fig1.svg)

Extend the four sloping side edges downward past the square bottom to complete a square pyramid. Sections parallel to its base have side lengths proportional to their distances from the apex, by similar triangles.

Let \(h>0\) be the distance from the apex to the container's bottom. Since the bottom and top square side lengths are \(1\) and \(3\), the top is \(3h\) from the apex. The container therefore has height \(2h\). Each trapezoid's midline joins the midpoints of its sloping edges, so the water surface is halfway up the container. It is \(2h\) from the apex and is a square of side length \(2\).

The three nested pyramids ending at the bottom, water surface, and top are similar, with linear scales \(1:2:3\). Scaling every length by a factor \(k\) scales volume by \(k^3\), so their volumes are in the ratio
\[
1^3:2^3:3^3=1:8:27.
\]
Let the smallest pyramid have volume \(V>0\). The water already added occupies the difference between the middle and smallest pyramids, namely \(8V-V=7V\). The remaining space occupies \(27V-8V=19V\).

If \(t\) is the additional filling time in minutes, constant flow gives
\[
\frac{t}{35}=\frac{19V}{7V}=\frac{19}{7}.
\]
Thus
\[
t=35\cdot\frac{19}{7}=\boxed{95}\text{ minutes},
\]
which is choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
